description: Core shared library for FlyOS business app integration. Provides multi-tenancy, authentication, authorization (Cerbos), Redis caching, OpenTelemetry, structured API response models, and ASP.NET Core middleware for building FlyOS-compatible microservices.
releaseNotes:
1.34.0: ITasksClient gains DeclareAppSlaTemplatesAsync(request) — the missing wrapper over the Tasks service's new PUT /api/sla-templates/app/{appId}, the inter-service surface where an app declares the SLA templates it ships as master data. There is no separate appId parameter: the endpoint's CheckOwningApp gate accepts only the caller's own inter-service identity, which TasksClientOptions.AppId already pins for every other call on this client. New DeclareAppSlaTemplatesRequest / AppSlaTemplateDeclarationRequest / AppSlaEventRequest / AppSlaEventActionRequest / AppSlaViolationLevelRequest mirror the Tasks service's request records field-for-field, and SlaClientTriggerType / SlaClientActionType / SlaClientActionTarget mirror the Tasks.Enums.Sla* enums the same way the existing TaskClient* enums mirror the Task-domain ones. Full-set semantics: the payload is the app's COMPLETE declared set on every call — any currently-active declaration for that app absent from it is soft-withdrawn server-side (never deleted), and a null Templates list is NOT "leave it alone", it reconciles to "withdraw everything". Each template must set exactly one of DurationMinutes / DurationBusinessDays (and every nested event offset must agree with that unit) or the whole call is rejected before anything is written (INVALID_DURATION / INVALID_EVENT_OFFSET); a repeated SysName fails with DUPLICATE. Returns AppSlaTemplateReconcileResult {Declared, Reactivated, Withdrawn}. Additive on ITasksClient; an out-of-repo implementor must add the member.
1.33.0: AddFlyCore() now refuses to start a Production host whose IDistributedCache is not actually distributed. UPGRADE NOTE — this can fail a boot that succeeds today: a Production service resolving the in-process MemoryDistributedCache (the AddDistributedMemoryCache() fallback), or registering no IDistributedCache at all, will now throw at startup instead of running on a per-pod cache. Fix it by registering Redis (AddStackExchangeRedisCache) and making sure the deployment sets Redis:ConnectionString, or set Redis:AllowInMemoryFallback=true if the deployment genuinely runs exactly one replica (the waiver logs a Warning; it never passes silently). Why it is worth a breaking boot: the in-memory fallback satisfies the IDistributedCache interface without being distributed, so each replica gets a private dictionary and every cross-request value — export and report byte caches, job result handoffs, at-least-once dedupe keys, leases, rate-limit counters, one-time download tokens — misses at a rate of 1 - 1/replicas. Nothing logs it, no health check fails, and every test host passes because it is one process, so the defect is invisible until a second replica exists. PPM shipped exactly that to stg: its status-pack export job cached the rendered pack in the memory of whichever pod consumed the job while the browser's download GET was load-balanced across replicas, producing an intermittent 404 for a document that had rendered perfectly. The guard reads the RESOLVED registration rather than the config key on purpose — a config check would have cleared the calendar service, which was handed Redis:ConnectionString and never read it. Development, Testing and Staging environments keep the fallback untouched.
1.32.0: the files-manager "scanner updating" window is now a typed, catchable outcome. files-manager refuses user-originated uploads with 503 + SCANNER_UPDATING + Retry-After while the malware scanner is briefly unreachable (a ClamAV signature reload or a clamd restart) rather than accepting them into quarantine behind a scanner that is not running. FilesClient promotes exactly that failure to the new Fly.Sdk.Core.Files.ScannerUnavailableException, which DERIVES from FilesClientException (unsealed for this) so every existing `catch (FilesClientException)` sees the same failures it always did and only callers that add a narrower catch change behaviour. The exception carries SuggestedDelay — the server's Retry-After when it sent one, else the new FileScanRetry.DefaultScannerRetryDelay (120 s, mirroring the server's Files:VirusScan:RetryAfterSeconds default). FileScanRetry also gains ScannerUpdatingCode, ScannerUpdatingStatus and the case-insensitive IsScannerUpdating(ex) classifier, which matches on the ERROR CODE only and never on a bare 503 — a codeless 503 is far more often the gateway, a rolling pod or a draining load balancer, and calling that "the scanner is updating" would tell the caller something the response never said. There is deliberately no auto-retrying upload overload: retrying an upload means re-sending the body, and FileUploadRequest.Content is a caller-owned stream that may not be rewindable, so a helper that quietly re-read it would send a truncated file — the caller owns the stream, so the caller owns the retry. Uploads an inter-service caller flags ServiceGenerated are never gated (they take the confirm fast-path and never reach the scanner). Additive: no consumer change is required to keep compiling or to keep today's behaviour.
1.27.0: UpdateTaskInterServiceRequest gains AssigneeIds (IReadOnlyList<Guid>?) and ReplaceAllAssignees (bool, default false), mirroring the Tasks service's A14 seam fix on PATCH /api/tasks/app/{appId}/{taskId}. AssigneeIds is the assignee SET the calling app declares for the task: null = don't touch assignees, [] = clear the assignees this inter-service path manages; Guid.Empty entries are ignored and duplicates collapse. The server reconciles rather than replays: audiences authored elsewhere (admin OU/role targeting, multi-user audiences) and their derived assignments survive untouched, new assignees go through the canonical materializer (TaskAssignedToUser publishes, delegation rules apply), and re-sending the same set is free. When both are sent, AssigneeIds wins over the legacy AssigneeId — which now routes through the same reconcile, so Guid.Empty clears the managed set rather than wiping everything. ReplaceAllAssignees=true is the opt-in blunt mode that deletes EVERY audience and assignment first (including admin-authored) before materializing the declared set — only for apps that own the task's entire assignment surface. Additive: both fields sit at the end of the record with safe defaults, so existing positional callers compile unchanged with unchanged meaning.
1.26.0: ITasksClient gains UpdateAsync(taskId, request) — the missing wrapper over PATCH /api/tasks/app/{appId}/{taskId}. Until now the client could create, read, comment on and bulk-mutate tasks by source but not update ONE task, so every app that needed to move a board card (status, title, description, start/due dates, assignee, source-entity relink) hand-rolled HTTP against the endpoint (strategies and PPM both did). UpdateTaskInterServiceRequest mirrors the server's InterServiceUpdateTaskRequest field-for-field: null = keep; Status is a tenant status NAME applied through the audited transition path (INVALID_STATUS on an unknown name, EXTERNAL_COMPLETION_ONLY on an externally-completed task); Description follows empty-string-clear; StartDate/DueDate are validated as an effective pair; AssigneeId = Guid.Empty unassigns; SourceEntityType/SourceEntityId must be supplied together to relink. Returns the new TaskByEntityRow (mirroring TaskByEntityIdDto, with TaskAssigneeInfo assignee rows) — the same shape the batch by-source query emits — or null on 404 (not found / not owned), matching GetAsync. Additive on ITasksClient; an out-of-repo implementor must add the member.
1.24.0: a missing Frontend:RemoteEntry is no longer silent. When an app declares an ExposedModule but does not configure Frontend:RemoteEntry, FlyAppRegistrationPayloads falls back to the SAMPLE TEMPLATE's federation port — so the app registers a catalog row that reads as healthy and fails only when the shell tries to open it. FlyAppRegistrationWorker now logs a Warning (EventId 5410, PlaceholderRemoteEntry) naming the app, the exposed module and the placeholder; a genuinely headless External App declares no ExposedModule and stays silent. Also 1.24.0: inter-service app surfaces finally work for External Apps. OwningAppGuard.CheckOwningApp compared the token's client_id to the route appId exactly, but only a Core App's confidential client carries the bare app id — an External App's is minted as `{appId}-service` by AppBootstrapController (its bare id is the public PKCE client). Every External App was therefore 403 APP_MISMATCH on every `.../app/{appId}` surface (Tasks, Chats, Calendar meetings, Projects); it stayed hidden because the pilot External App published to Tasks over the message bus instead of calling the HTTP surface. Ownership is now the shared predicate Fly.Sdk.Core.Auth.AppClientIds.Owns — exactly two accepted forms, bare and `-service`, ordinal — and AppClientIds (ServiceClientSuffix, ForService, HasServiceClientSuffix, Owns) is the single home for the convention that the Controller's bootstrap/onboarding/role-binding gates and the Comments brokered-write gate now all consume, so a rename cannot re-open the gap on one side. Tightening shipped with it: an app id ending in `-service` is refused at bootstrap and denied at the gate (new OwningAppGuard.ReservedAppIdCode = APP_ID_RESERVED), because app `x`'s inter-service client id is indistinguishable from an app named `x-service` — an escalation path a bare exact-match comparison already had. No platform app id ends in the suffix. Deny messages now name both ids AND the two accepted forms.
1.23.0: IControllerClient gains ResolveUsersAsync(tenantId, userIds) — bulk-resolve user ids to display identity + email over Controller's existing POST /api/internal/users/resolve (max 200/call), with the same graceful-empty-on-error contract as the other client methods. Enables inter-service callers (e.g. the Calendar meeting surface) to resolve attendee emails. Additive; NoOpControllerClient returns empty in standalone mode.
1.22.0: forwarded-headers trust is now enforceable. AddFlyServiceDefaults routes ForwardedHeadersOptions through the new public ForwardedHeadersConfigurator — set ForwardedHeaders:TrustedProxyNetworks (CIDRs) / :TrustedProxies (IPs) and it pins KnownIPNetworks/KnownProxies to the real Front-Door + ingress egress ranges AND pins ForwardLimit (default 2) so RemoteIpAddress is the real client and X-Forwarded-For is trusted ONLY from those proxies up to the pinned hop count. This closes the P0.5 gateway finding where clearing the known-lists silently trusted one XFF hop from ANY peer (shared-egress rate-limit bucket + client-spoofable). Unconfigured (dev/local) preserves the historical clear-both behavior byte-for-byte; no consumer change unless you opt in via the new keys. 1.21.0: tenant-wide file read is finally reversible. IFilesClient gains RevokeTenantReadAsync(fileId) and IFileReferences gains the bulk RevokeTenantReadAsync(ids), both idempotent, backed by the new files-manager route DELETE /api/file-permissions/tenant-read/{fileId}. Until now an app that opened tenant-wide read on publish had no way to close it again when the entity was hidden, so anyone who captured the file id kept downloading it; consumers were carrying TODO markers instead of a fix. Revoke authorization deliberately mirrors the grant (owner-or-admin plus a Cerbos share:revoke gate) — only the wildcard ALLOW rows on the file are removed, so wildcard deny rows, user/OU grants and folder-inherited grants are untouched. 1.20.0: a best-effort bootstrap (BootstrapRequired=false) now RETRIES in the background instead of getting a single shot. Previously a rung-0 failure caused by ordering — the Controller's Apps:RegistrationToken landing after the app pod booted — was permanent and silent: register/onboard/heartbeat still succeeded so /api/services stayed Healthy, while the app's SPA had no working login (ID2052 at /connect/authorize) until someone manually restarted the pod. The retry loop runs CONCURRENTLY with the rest of the ladder (it never gates it) and self-heals the moment the Controller-side cause is fixed; recovery emits the new BootstrapRecovered (5403) EventId, so alerting on "5401 with no following 5403" catches a bootstrap that never came back. 1.19.0: the app-registration ladder is now LOUD — per-rung FlyAppRegistrationState with fly.app.registration.* gauges, an app-registration health check (opt-in readiness gating via FailReadinessOnRegistrationFailure), and structured-EventId Error logging on bootstrap 4xx/5xx + worker fatal stop. 1.18.0: canonical Fly.Sdk.Core.Models.PagedResult<T> record (wire field 'total') is now the one shared paged envelope; the legacy PagedResponse<T> (wire field 'totalCount') is [Obsolete] but retained as a compile shim.
